feature: Customer Portal v2 Part 6 -- Reference -> SOPs & Runbooks (/portal-v2/sops) and its four sop-* category pages. Recreated from the prototype's own `isSopHub` block ('Customer Portal Shell.dc.html' 1633-1978) and its SOP_LIBRARY / SOP_META / SOP_QUEUE / SOP_AUDIT derivations, transcribed into sopHubData.ts + sopHubModel.ts and pinned by unit assertions. The hub has three sub-views -- library / execution queue / execution history -- each a real linkable URL (base = library, /sops/queue, /sops/audit) and a shell-nav sub-item under SOPs & Runbooks. The library is a master-detail: a grouped, filterable index on the left and the selected procedure in full on the right, with an execution slide-over for runnable procedures. The four category keys (incident-response / security-drift / mail-flow / device-mgmt) are the prototype's `sopCategories` (shell 8789), which the design renders through its generic placeholder branch (shell 6500-6507) -- reproduced faithfully as real, linkable routes. UI-only: every value is the design's own fixture, so these steps assert rendered design copy rather than an endpoint.
notes: THE LOGIN BLOCK IS NOT OPTIONAL. /portal-v2/* sits behind ProtectedRoute; a probe that skips the five login steps hits the login screen and every assertion fails for a reason unrelated to the page.

UI ROUTE SHAPE: msp-portal's outer WouterRouter has base '/portal' and SlugScope nests a second router at '/{slug}', so the real URL is /portal/{slug}/portal-v2/sops. App.tsx declares the four /sops/<category> routes BEFORE '/sops/:view' (the queue/audit param) and both before '/portal-v2/:pillar' so nothing is swallowed.
shaneapp://runTest hits the DEPLOYED build, not the local worktree; this manifest needs the Part 6 pages deployed first.

PERSISTED-SESSION FLAKE (known): when WebView2 is already authed, the two input steps against #email/#password can fail while the rest runs green because auth persists. N-2 of N with only those two red is a PASS for the feature.

THIS PAGE IS UI-ONLY. There is no apiTests block beyond the login setup -- there is no SOP endpoint yet; a later pass wires it. These steps assert that the design's copy and structure render, which is what the fidelity audit cannot check on its own.

THE EXECUTE BUTTONS open the execution slide-over directly. In the prototype they route through the change-request gate (a shell system owned by another part); UI-only here, so the drawer -- the design's real execution surface -- opens directly.
ENV VARS required in BuildConsole -> Settings -> Test Environment Variables: DEPLOY_URL, TEST_PORTAL_EMAIL / TEST_PORTAL_PASSWORD.
